panels.name: Swap memory used
panels.description: High swap use can degrade I/O performance. If memory is available, review the host swappiness setting.

panels.name: OOM kills per second
panels.description: A value above zero means the kernel killed a process because memory was exhausted.

panels.name: File descriptor utilization
panels.description: Sustained utilization above 80% requires a higher system file descriptor limit or reduced workload.

panels.name: CPU utilization
panels.description: Sustained high utilization can indicate an abnormal process or insufficient host capacity.

panels.name: Memory utilization
panels.description: Sustained high utilization can indicate that the service or host needs more memory.

panels.name: Processes running
panels.description: A persistently high runnable process count can indicate host saturation.

panels.name: Available entropy
panels.description: A depleted entropy pool can block consumers of kernel randomness.

panels.name: Direct mapped memory
panels.description: DirectMap values show how much memory is mapped with each page size and help assess TLB efficiency.
